page: Google Cloud Platform h4d-standard-192 is an x86_64 architecture server instance featuring 192 dedicated virtual CPUs and 720.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a memory allocation of 3.75 GB per virtual core. The instance does not include any integrated GPUs, and local storage is not bundled, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes.

Operating on a dedicated CPU allocation model, the h4d-standard-192 provides predictable compute resources without resource contention. The lack of local NVMe storage and integrated GPU hardware represents a clear tradeoff, positioning this instance for workloads that rely heavily on external storage systems and CPU-bound processing. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of dedicated vCPUs and balanced memory allocation offers a consolidated platform for large-scale deployments, reducing the overhead of managing multiple smaller instances.

This server type is designed for highly parallelized workloads that scale efficiently across a large number of CPU cores. Suitable applications include large-scale web serving, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines, enterprise application hosting, and distributed data processing tasks that do not require local disk caching or GPU acceleration.
